record.paper_title: Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces in the Unit Ball: Recent Advances and Open Questions
record.original_question: Fix a compact surface Σ with boundary and a prescribed topological type, and let g range over smooth Riemannian metrics on Σ. For each positive integer k, what is the exact sharp upper bound of the normalized k-th Steklov eigenvalue σ_k(g)|∂Σ|_g for that topological type? Moreover, is this sharp upper bound attained by some smooth metric on Σ rather than only as a supremum over metrics?

evidence.quote: Open Question 2 (Fraser-Schoen [30]). For each topological type of Σ, what is the sharp upper bound for σ_k(g)|∂Σ|_g? Is it achieved by a smooth metric on Σ?
These are called the Steklov eigenvalues of (Σ, g).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Σ be a smooth compact surface with non-empty boundary, of a fixed topological type (specified by its orientability, genus γ, and number of boundary components b). For a smooth Riemannian metric g on Σ, the Steklov eigenvalue problem consists in finding all real numbers σ such that there exists a non-zero function u ∈ C^∞(Σ) satisfying

  Δ_g u = 0 in Σ,    ∂u/∂ν = σ u on ∂Σ,

where ν is the outward unit conormal to ∂Σ. The eigenvalues form a discrete sequence

  0 = σ_0(g) < σ_1(g) ≤ σ_2(g) ≤ ⋯ → ∞.

Let |∂Σ|_g denote the length of ∂Σ in the metric g. For each positive integer k, define

  Σ_k^*(Σ) := sup_{g} σ_k(g) · |∂Σ|_g,

where the supremum is taken over all smooth Riemannian metrics g on Σ.

(a) Determine the exact value of Σ_k^*(Σ) in terms of the topological type of Σ and of k.

(b) Decide whether the supremum Σ_k^*(Σ) is attained by some smooth Riemannian metric g on Σ, or whether it is realized only as a limit (e.g. by a degenerating sequence of metrics).
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem remains open. Sharp values are known only in a few special cases: for the disk (γ=0, b=1), Σ_k^* = 2πk (Hersch–Payne–Schiffer / Girouard–Polterovich); for the annulus (γ=0, b=2) and k=1, the sharp bound is realized by the critical catenoid (Fraser–Schoen). Existence/regularity of maximizers in many topological types has been established (Fraser–Schoen, Petrides, Matthiesen–Petrides), but explicit sharp constants for general (γ, b, k) are not known, and recent surveys list this as an outstanding open question.

status_evidence.title: Some recent developments on the Steklov Eigenvalue Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys sharp Steklov bounds; sharp values known only in special topological types, with general case open.
status_evidence.claim: The sharp value of the normalized k-th Steklov eigenvalue is known only in special topological cases.

status_evidence.title: Spectral geometry of the Steklov problem
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses upper bounds σ_k L(∂Σ) ≤ 2(2γ+k)π and notes sharpness only for limited cases.
status_evidence.claim: General sharp bounds and attainment by smooth metrics are not fully resolved.
